# Example Org — Authentication & Credential Management Operational Procedure

## Purpose

Executing this procedure implements the identification, authentication, authenticator management, session management, and system use notification requirements of the Example Org Authentication & Credential Management Standard, so that only uniquely identified and authenticated users, processes, and devices gain access to Example Org systems and electronic protected health information.

## Scope

IAM Engineering performs this procedure continuously across all Example Org systems that authenticate users, processes, or devices, including the [Identity Provider], [Directory Service], [MDM Solution], [Ticketing System], and all applications that grant access based on authenticated sessions.

## Prerequisites

- Administrative access to the [Identity Provider] and [Directory Service] for configuring lockout, session, and authentication policies.
- Administrative access to the [MDM Solution] for device lock, wipe, and biometric configuration.
- Access to the [Ticketing System] for logging lockout releases, authenticator changes, and exception requests.
- The applicable System Security and Privacy Plan(s) defining all organization-defined values referenced below (session limits, re-authentication circumstances, logout messages, device lists, lease durations, and similar).
- Capability to generate the MFA enrolment report and the Authentication policy configuration export.
- Access to the [Password Screening Tool] and the source feed for the compromised password list.
- Access to the [Certificate Authority] / [PKI Management Console] for public key and trust store management.
- The current list of General Services Administration-approved identity, credential, and access management products and services.

## Procedure Steps

### 1. Enforce Invalid Logon Attempt Limits and Account Lockout [NIST AC-7 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

1. Open the [Identity Provider] administrative console and set the invalid logon threshold to five (5) consecutive invalid attempts within a fifteen (15) minute period, per ARC-AMPE.
1. Configure the lockout action to lock the account or node for a minimum of thirty (30) minutes; where the System Security and Privacy Plan requires administrator release instead, set the lock to persist until released by an administrator.
1. Configure the [Identity Provider] to notify the system administrator (via the [Ticketing System] or [Security Operations] alerting channel) when the maximum unsuccessful logon attempts is exceeded.
1. Where the plan specifies an alternative action (logon prompt delay algorithm or other organization-defined action), configure it in the [Identity Provider] exactly as documented in the plan.
1. Generate the Authentication policy configuration export and retain it as evidence that the threshold, time period, and lockout action are in force.

### 2. Purge Mobile Devices After Unsuccessful Logon Attempts [NIST AC-7(2) | ARC-AMPE AC-7(2) AE Mandatory]

1. In the [MDM Solution], identify the mobile devices subject to purging or wiping as defined in the System Security and Privacy Plan.
1. Configure the device wipe policy to trigger after ten (10) consecutive unsuccessful device logon attempts, per ARC-AMPE, using the purging/wiping techniques defined in the plan.
1. Apply the policy to the defined device group and confirm enrollment coverage in the [MDM Solution] device inventory.
1. Record the policy configuration in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### 3. Limit Biometric and Alternative-Factor Logon Attempts [NIST AC-7(3) | NIST AC-7(4)]

1. In the [Biometric Authentication System], set the limit on consecutive unsuccessful biometric logon attempts to [Biometric Attempt Limit].
1. In the [Identity Provider], configure the fallback authentication factors (different from the primary factors) that a user may use after the consecutive invalid logon attempt limit has been exceeded, as defined in the System Security and Privacy Plan.
1. Enforce a separate limit of [Alternative Factor Attempt Limit] consecutive invalid attempts through the alternative factors within [Alternative Factor Time Period].
1. Verify both limits by test authentication attempts and record the results in the [Ticketing System].

### 4. Display System Use Notification Banners [NIST AC-8 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

1. Obtain the approved system use notification text from the System Security and Privacy Plan, confirming it states that users are accessing a system containing U.S. Government information, that usage may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit, that unauthorized use is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties, and that use indicates consent to monitoring and recording.
1. Configure the banner in the [Identity Provider] login flow and on operating system login screens via the [Endpoint Management System] so it displays before access is granted.
1. Configure the banner to remain on screen until the user acknowledges the usage conditions and takes an explicit action to log on or further access the system; do not configure auto-dismissal.
1. For publicly accessible systems, configure the notification to display under the conditions defined in the System Security and Privacy Plan before granting further access, include a description of the authorized uses of the system, and align any references to monitoring, recording, or auditing with the privacy accommodations that generally prohibit those activities on such systems.

### 5. Verify System Use Notification Compliance [ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

1. Confirm with the System Owner the elements of the environment that require the System Use Notification control, how notification compliance will be verified, and the periodicity of the check.
1. If verification is performed as part of a configuration baseline check, include the banner settings in the baseline scan scope in [Configuration Management Tool].
1. If verification is not part of a baseline check, confirm a documented agreement exists covering how verification results are provided to the System Owner and the verification periodicity.
1. Execute the verification at the agreed periodicity and provide the results to the System Owner through the agreed channel.

### 6. Limit Concurrent Sessions [NIST AC-10 High | ARC-AMPE AC-10 AE Mandatory]

1. In the [Identity Provider] and [Application Platform], configure concurrent session limits for each account and account type to one (1) session, where a session is an encounter between an end-user interface device and an application, including a network logon.
1. For any account type requiring more than one (1) concurrent session, confirm the requirement is expressly needed for the performance of job duties and documented in the applicable security and privacy plan before raising the limit.
1. Record any raised limits and their plan documentation references in the [Ticketing System].

### 7. Enforce Device Lock and Session Concealment [NIST AC-11 Moderate, High | NIST AC-11(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-11 AE Mandatory]

1. Via the [MDM Solution] and [Endpoint Management Tool], configure the device lock to initiate after fifteen (15) minutes of inactivity, with inactivity covering both remote and internal access connections.
1. Configure and communicate the requirement that users initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended; ARC-AMPE requires both the timed lock and the user-initiated lock.
1. Configure the lock so it is retained until the user reestablishes access using established identification and authentication procedures (password, PIN, or biometric as applicable).
1. Set the lock screen to conceal all previously visible information with a publicly viewable image.
1. Verify the settings on a sample of endpoints and record the results in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### 8. Control Workstation Use and ePHI Access Authorization [HIPAA 164.310(b) | HIPAA 164.312(a)(1)]

1. Maintain, with the System Owner, documented policies and procedures specifying the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of each workstation or workstation class that can access electronic protected health information.
1. In the [Directory Service] and [Application Platform], implement technical policies and procedures so that systems maintaining electronic protected health information allow access only to those persons or software programs granted access rights as specified in § 164.308(a)(4).
1. Review workstation access group memberships against the § 164.308(a)(4) access grants and remove any mismatch through the [Ticketing System] access change process.

### 9. Provide Emergency ePHI Access and Encryption [HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(ii) Required | HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iv) Addressable]

1. Establish, and implement as needed, documented procedures for obtaining necessary electronic protected health information during an emergency; store the procedure with the applicable security and privacy plan documentation.
1. When an emergency access is invoked, follow the procedure and log the event, the requester, and the justification in the [Ticketing System].
1. Implement the [Encryption Mechanism] to encrypt and decrypt electronic protected health information at rest and in transit, using the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards for systems containing PII.

### 10. Terminate Sessions and Provide Logout Capability [NIST AC-12 Moderate, High | NIST AC-12(1) | NIST AC-12(2) | NIST AC-12(3) | ARC-AMPE AC-12, AC-12(1), AC-12(2), AC-12(3) AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iii) Addressable]

1. In the [Identity Provider] and each application handling authenticated sessions, configure automatic session termination after the trigger events defined in the System Security and Privacy Plan (e.g., periods of user inactivity, targeted responses to certain incident types, time-of-day restrictions), including an electronic procedure that terminates the session after the predetermined time of inactivity.
1. Configure a logout capability for user-initiated communications sessions on every information resource, as defined in the applicable security and privacy plans, wherever authentication is used to gain access.
1. Configure the explicit logout message documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (e.g., "Your session has been terminated") to display when an authenticated session is terminated.
1. Configure the session-end warning to display an explicit message indicating the session will end in [Time Until Session End], as specified in the applicable security and privacy plans.
1. Verify each setting by an authenticated test session and record the results in the Authentication policy configuration export.

### 11. Maintain the Identification and Authentication Policy and Procedures Documentation [NIST IA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.316(b)(1)(i) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)]

1. Develop and document the identification and authentication policy and supporting procedures in written (electronic permitted) form, addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, consistent with applicable laws, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
1. Disseminate the policy and procedures to the personnel or roles defined in the policy.
1. Confirm the official designated to manage development, documentation, and dissemination of the policy and procedures is named in the policy; if the designation has changed, update the policy through the document change process.
1. Review and update the policy and procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events such as assessment or audit findings, security or privacy incidents, or changes to applicable laws, directives, regulations, policies, standards, or guidelines; review periodically and update as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.
1. Retain all documentation produced under this procedure for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later.
1. Make the documentation available to the persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which it pertains, via the [Document Repository].

### 12. Uniquely Identify and Authenticate Organizational Users [NIST IA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-2 | ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(i) Required | HIPAA 164.312(d)]

1. Assign a unique name and/or number to each organizational user and to processes acting on their behalf, in the [Directory Service], for identifying and tracking user identity.
1. Perform identity proofing and authentication compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines document suite before issuing system and/or network authenticators and unique user identifiers.
1. Verify that each person or entity seeking access to electronic protected health information is the one claimed, using the proofed identity bound to the authenticator.
1. Require user identification for any help desk support transaction that has information security and privacy implications; instruct Help Desk staff to verify the requester's identity against the [Directory Service] before proceeding.

### 13. Implement Multi-Factor Authentication [NIST IA-2(1) Low, Moderate, High | NIST IA-2(2) Low, Moderate, High | NIST IA-2(5) High | NIST IA-2(6) | NIST IA-2(8) Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-2, IA-2(1), IA-2(2), IA-2(6), IA-2(8) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(1), IA-2(2), IA-2(5), IA-2(6), IA-2(8) AE Mandatory]

1. In the [Identity Provider], require multi-factor authentication using two or more different factors (something you know, something you have, or something you are) appropriate to the level of risk for all privileged accounts.
1. Require multi-factor authentication for all non-privileged account types per ARC-AMPE; note that MFA for consumer accounts is strongly recommended but not currently mandated.
1. Select only phishing-resistant MFA methods, in accordance with current CISA guidance, for new enrollments and replace non-compliant methods as they are identified.
1. For local, network, and remote access to privileged and non-privileged accounts, configure MFA such that one factor is provided by a device separate from the system gaining access and that device meets the latest published FIPS 140-compliant cryptography.
1. Configure replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for access to privileged and non-privileged accounts.
1. Where shared accounts or authenticators are employed, configure the workflow so each user is individually authenticated before access to the shared account or resource is granted.
1. Generate the MFA enrolment report from the [Identity Provider], reconcile it against the privileged and non-privileged account inventories, and remediate any unenrolled accounts through the [Ticketing System].

### 14. Provide Single Sign-On, PIV Acceptance, and Out-of-Band Authentication [NIST IA-2(10) | NIST IA-2(12) Low, Moderate, High | NIST IA-2(13)]

1. Configure single sign-on in the [Identity Provider] for the system accounts and services defined in the System Security and Privacy Plan.
1. Configure the federation endpoint to accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials.
1. Implement the out-of-band authentication mechanisms defined in the System Security and Privacy Plan, triggered under the conditions defined in that plan.

### 15. Identify and Authenticate Devices [NIST IA-3 Moderate, High | NIST IA-3(1) | NIST IA-3(3) | NIST IA-3(4) | ARC-AMPE IA-3 AE Mandatory]

1. Configure the [Network Access Control] system to uniquely identify and authenticate the devices and/or device types approved for identification and authentication management in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan before establishing a local, remote, or network connection; at a minimum, use authentication mechanisms based on shared information (MAC or IP address) and access control lists to control remote network access.
1. Configure bidirectional, cryptographically based authentication for the devices and/or device types requiring it before any local, remote, or network connection is established.
1. Where addresses are allocated dynamically, standardize dynamic address allocation lease information and lease duration in accordance with [Lease Information and Duration], and audit lease information each time it is assigned to a device via the [DHCP Service] logs.
1. Where device identification and authentication is based on attestation, configure it to rely on the [Configuration Management Process] as the attesting authority.

### 16. Manage Authenticator Distribution and Lifecycle [NIST IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

1. As part of initial authenticator distribution, verify the identity of the individual, group, role, service, or device receiving the authenticator before issuing it.
1. Establish initial authenticator content for any authenticators issued by the organization; change default authenticators (including vendor-supplied passwords) prior to first use and immediately upon system installation.
1. Maintain administrative procedures, held with the policy documentation, covering initial authenticator distribution, lost or compromised or damaged authenticators, and revocation of authenticators; execute them via the [Ticketing System].
1. Change or refresh authenticators per the time period defined by authenticator type in [Authenticator Refresh Period] and when the defined events occur; change authenticators immediately when they are no longer valid due to known or suspected compromise.
1. Confirm each authenticator has sufficient strength of mechanism for its intended use, including compliance with the most recent
